10/10 for this clinic! My yorkie Chloe had a pretty large lump on her belly, so I brought her to Furever Friends Animal Hosptial in Hialeah to find out what it could be.  It turned out to be an incisional hernia.   The good thing is that this clinic is not overpriced like some others. The explain exactly what Chloe had and showed me what they were going to do to fix it.

On the day of the surgery, they called me to keep me updated on everything they were doing with CHLOE.  They also called me with her lab results and let me know that everything looked good for her have the surgery.  The surgeon himself spoke with me after the surgery and explained how everything went. It went really good.

The next day, they called me to check on how Chloe had done overnight and contito make sure she was doing well. Honestly, I feel like even some human doctors don’t provide that level of care and communication.

I,m definitely going to continue bringing my Chloe here and my others pets.  I highly recommend this furever friends Animal.

This is by far the worst veterinary clinic I have ever experienced. They only care about making money and have no sense of ethics or compassion. Instead of putting the animals' well-being first, they make decisions based on what is most convenient and profitable for them. I would never recommend this place to anyone who truly cares about their pet.

I find it contradictory that you now claim your recommendation was based on my pet's history of epilepsy and avoiding medications that could cause neurological effects. The very day my dog ​​was diagnosed with epilepsy, you yourselves prescribed a medication that Chewy later identified as potentially risky due to his condition. It was Chewy, who is not his veterinarian and was simply processing the prescription, who had to contact you to warn you about this.

After that warning, you called me to inform me and changed the prescription. However, you subsequently prescribed another medication that also presented risks related to his condition. Therefore, my concern is not based on disagreeing with a medical recommendation, nor is it solely about money. My concern is that, knowing my dog's epilepsy diagnosis, medications that could pose a risk to him were recommended.

Doctors and everyone of the staff members are absolutely amazing. Everything is thoroughly explained throughout the entire process, if there is any sort of change you are alerted right away. Care for the animals is top priority for this team, and that is why they will always be my go-to!

I arrived and they gave me a list of tests, and I said it was too much for me. Then the "veterinarian" started removing things from the list that he said weren't necessary. Afterward, the "veterinarian" was going to gossip with his employees if I told the truth about some information a girl at the front desk, who is more professional than him, had given me.

Then they treated me like a thief because they locked me in until I paid the other girl at the front desk who works the afternoon shift. These people had no consideration for the pain of my 8-year-old daughter, who witnessed the whole thing, just because I couldn't afford a treatment that cost over $3,000 and wanted to seek help. I assure you, these individuals have neither professional ethics nor human decency.

I've been taking my pets there for over 7 years, and although they weren't fancy, the veterinarian, Dr. Dayana Sosa, was the reason we went. Regretfully, she sold her practice to the worst veterinarian I've ever met.

He lacks bedside manners and never explains what he is doing or plans to do. He misdiagnosed my dog and blamed it on arthritis because he doesn't listen. He would have discovered that she had bone cancer if he had truly examined the x-rays.

He expected me to understand what I was looking at when he showed me the x-rays, which were not even labeled, so I had no way of knowing which was left or right. Condescending and sarcastic, he gestured toward the screen as though I could see what I was looking at. I asked him, "Would you care to explain this?  I have no idea what you're pointing at." He drew in a sharp breath as if I was bothering him by asking. He then told me that she had advanced arthritis, and he gave her a shot for pain and prescribed 3 medications. I told him that she had a mass removed 6 months prior and that I was concerned about a lump in her leg. He never looked into it or reviewed her previous medical issues. Instead, he charged me $560 and sent me on my merry way.

Three weeks later she was so much worse. I wasn't about to take her back. I searched for another vet, and he told me that the x-rays were so bad that he couldn't really treat her without redoing them. His X-rays were clear, and even I could see what Dr. Goldberg completely missed. My girl died 4 months later, and I could have done more in that 1 month that I lost from his negligence.

Osteosarcoma is the worst and most painful of the cancers. You can say all you want, but I could have had her leg amputated, and she would have been able to last a year or 2. If you dont believe me and your dog has bone ancer, I have so many possibilities to share with you, but what I will say is STAY AWAY FROM THIS SORRY EXCUSE FOR A VET.
